messages:
oncall_incident_bot: ALERT: Streaming tail-latency p95/p99 spike detected for SSE endpoints in eu-west-1. Trigger: p99 > 10s for 3 consecutive mins. Incident ID: INC-2026-0452. Pager: @pager_duty.

maria_sre: I’m on it — can someone grab top-level metrics (proxy write latency, socket counts, client timeouts)?

sam_dev: saw the first uptick at 12:03 UTC. proxy-write-queue latency jumps correlate with a spike in slow consumers on stream-proxy-2/3.

kevin_infra: kernel logs on proxy-2 show a lot of TCP retransmits + keepalive retries. Also seeing write syscall backpressure in strace (blocked writes).

jen_prod: customer impact — any evidence of dropped sessions or error responses to callers? Need list of affected tenants so support can contact.

lisa_support: two customers (org-acme, org-halo) filed tickets: "responses stalling for 8-12s then resume". They reported multiple reconnects. Ticket IDs: TKT-987, TKT-990.

maria_sre: quick query: p95 from baseline ~200ms -> 3.2s at peak; p99 ~12s. Affected endpoints: /v1/stream/generate (SSE) and websocket fallback.

sam_dev: probable root cause candidates: client backpressure (slow readers), proxy write timeout too generous causing head-of-line blocking, and a recently rolled kernel tuning on proxy-3 that changed TCP socket buffers.

kevin_infra: mitigation option 1: enable per-conn write pacing + short write timeout to fail noisy slow-consumers earlier (config snippet below). Option 2: route traffic away from eu-west-1 to eu-north-1 (capacity limited). Prefer quick config change canary first.

kevin_infra: ```
# proxy config patch (canary on 2 hosts)
proxy.write_timeout: 10s   # down from 30s
proxy.chunk_window_ms: 50 # reduce buffered chunk window
proxy.enable_per_connection_pacing: true
```

pager_duty: deploying canary patch to stream-proxy-2 and stream-proxy-4 now. Will monitor p95/p99 and socket backlog. @maria_sre please watch tracing for KV cache thrash.

customer_ops: notifying org-acme & org-halo that we're investigating; advising to expect transient stalls during mitigation.

maria_sre: placed tracing flags on a few sample requests to capture chunking behavior and per-connection buffer metrics. Also started tcpdump on proxy-2 for 2 minutes.

oncall_incident_bot: DEPLOY STARTED: canary/patch-1812345678 by pager_duty at 12:12:05 UTC.

pager_duty: canary applied to proxy-2 (done) and proxy-4 (done). Watching metrics.

sam_dev: early signs good — proxy write latency per-host down by ~60% on canaries, socket backlog decreasing.

lisa_support: customers report improvement: "stalls reduced, still occasional 1-2s pauses" (org-acme).

maria_sre: metrics update at 12:17 UTC: p95 ~260ms, p99 ~1.6s. Error counts for SSE 5xx unchanged. No mass reconnects.

jen_prod: good first step. Next: roll to rest of proxies in eu-west-1 over 10m with progressive ramp and keep an eye on client-side reconnect rates.

kevin_infra: rolling to remaining proxies now with 30s interval. Will revert immediately if any increase in 5xx.

pager_duty: roll complete. oncall check: p95 stable at 240-300ms, p99 ~1.5-1.8s. socket retransmit rates dropping.

maria_sre: marking incident as mitigated. Root cause hypothesis: a combination of kernel tuning change on one host and too-large proxy write timeout which allowed slow readers to accumulate buffered writes and cause head-of-line blocking across multiplexed connections. Client backpressure amplified the problem.

customer_ops: confirming with customers — org-acme marks incident resolved, org-halo observed improved UX.

jen_prod: ACTIONS: (1) postmortem (owner: maria_sre) due EOD; (2) revert kernel tuning on proxy-3 and validate defaults (owner: kevin_infra); (3) add regression alert for streaming p99 > 5s (owner: sam_dev); (4) consider reducing default proxy.write_timeout and enable pacing by default (owner: infra-team).

maria_sre: assigning postmortem. Will include timeline, traces, tcpdump snippets, and customer impact table.

pager_duty: closing paging rotation — handing back to regular oncall. Thanks all. :handshake:

lisa_support: will follow up with formal customer communications and postmortem link when ready. :email:
